findings.text: ai.pattern_mood.sonnet.v1 leads to date: 59 trades, 30 wins, net +157.17 USD after costs (0.27%), the only strategy with a usable sample and a positive total. This week it lost: 39 trades, 15 wins, -165.33 USD (-0.42%). The lead is small and unproven; these inputs hold no luck test.

Both baselines lost after costs: base.always_up.v1 646 trades, 314 wins, -2661.63 USD (-0.41%); base.momentum.v1 341 trades, -1212.46 USD (-0.36%). The week's biggest misses were company-specific drops (META, GM), the biggest wins sector lifts (PGR, CVX); the end-of-day note says news explained none of the move in any item.

Rule strategies are too thin to judge: at most 7 trades (rule.model_news_double.v1, -59.57 USD). rule.model_news_confirmed.v1, rule.model_news_half.v1, rule.model_news_high.v1 and base.model_only.v1 each have one trade at -77.65 USD, the net of the BAC pick where news explained most of the move; rule.model_news.v1 and ai.combined.sonnet.v1 match at -80.25 USD. One-parameter comparisons cannot separate yet.

Promotional analyst items were followed by negative abnormal returns: -0.665% at 3 days (interval -1.18 to -0.15, 136 events) and -0.91% at 5 days (-1.65 to -0.18). The benchmark fell about as much (-0.74%, -1.12%) and the event windows overlap, so this one week is no evidence for a new news weight.

Verified news is too thin to judge: no confirmed_primary or corroborated row has enough events yet; earnings confirmed_primary had 1 event, and analyst single_source medium had 10 events with intervals spanning zero (3 days: +0.80%, -0.67 to 2.28). The NVDA lesson fits: one corroborated story did not stop a losing call.
